questions.text: Read the problem statement and imagine your target customers. Start by understanding the given problem. Then, identify the issues to be addressed. Think of ideas and sketch a prototype on paper. Finally, show how it solves the problem and suggest improvements. You may use the answer sheets in either portrait or landscape mode. Follow the same mode throughout. Do NOT exceed 10 pages. [IMAGE: /data/images/ms4002_2026T2_ET_FN_p2_Im1.webp|block] Using the Karmic Design Thinking (KDT) framework, complete the following: 1. Identify who you are designing for, and what is missing because people are never bored anymore. Explain why it matters now, and list the problems to solve. 2. Synthesize insights and articulate what core conflict users face and develop 2-3 How Might We questions that opens space for solution ideas. 3. Suggest 3-5 product ideas and then choose one primary concept. Explain how your product brings boredom back and how you would create an experience that is engaging because it is boring. Describe the trade-offs you would make. 4. Draw a simple sketch of the designed product or service (No visual polish needed, focus on clarity and flow.) 5. Briefly describe the iterations, and what success looks like. Suggest how you would measure “boredom achieved.” Guidelines: • What do you mean by “people experience boredom in a meaningful way”? Boredom means allowing moments of “nothing much happening,” and intentional stillness. It does not mean a lack of purpose or repetitive monotony. The goal is to create space that may enable creativity, imagination, and happiness. • What kind of product or service needs to be designed? It can be physical or digital, such as an app, device, system, process, or flow. Your design should clearly connect to the given problem. • Who can you design for? You can choose any domain, and any target customers. Make reasonable assumptions about your target customers. Your approach should be human-centred.

questions.text: In KDT - Customer Journey Mapping (CJM), why is it critical to explicitly document the user's emotional state alongside their physical actions?
options: To construct a compelling fictional backstory for user personas to make stakeholder presentations more engaging.
To quantify the exact emotion during each task so the development team can optimize product development.
To identify friction, and moments of delight, revealing latent needs for design intervention.
To gather positive emotional narratives that can be directly extracted and used for social media marketing campaigns.
questions.correct_answer: To identify friction, and moments of delight, revealing latent needs for design intervention.

questions.text: Which of the following tools and frameworks are used in combination during the Analyze phase of Karmic Design Thinking? 1. Multi-Why Analysis 2. Conflict of Interest mapping 3. IF-THEN-BUT framing 4. HMW questions 5. Multi-Way Analysis Select the correct option using the codes given below:
In the context of the Karmic Design Thinking process, what is the primary objective of "bulletproofing" before moving into full-scale prototype development?
options: To completely eliminate all potential risks and uncertainties associated with a proposed solution.
To strengthen preliminary analysis and solutions by rigorously evaluating their feasibility and desirability against real-world constraints.
To refine the visual aesthetics and surface-level appeal of a prototype to ensure high user engagement.
To accelerate the implementation phase by bypassing early-stage constraint analysis and obstacle identification.
questions.correct_answer: To strengthen preliminary analysis and solutions by rigorously evaluating their feasibility and desirability against real-world constraints.

questions.text: In the context of the KDT process, the Test phase is primarily categorized as what type of thinking activity?
options: Convergent (evaluating and narrowing down to validate a solution)
Linear (moving only forward without looking back)
questions.correct_answer: Convergent (evaluating and narrowing down to validate a solution)

When embarking on website development, how does the choice of a specific site-building platform primarily impact the project lifecycle?
options: It strictly mandates which third-party marketing services must be integrated.
It guarantees the website’s automatic visibility and engagement on social media networks.
It independently determines the website's final organic ranking on search engines.
It influences the technical ease of use, built-in feature availability, and the limits of design customization.
questions.correct_answer: It influences the technical ease of use, built-in feature availability, and the limits of design customization.

questions.text: A user interacts with an online ticketing app. They experience frustration during the complex seat- selection process, but checking out is incredibly smooth, and the app displays a delightful, celebratory animation upon securing the ticket. Based on Kahneman’s Peak-End Rule, how is the user most likely to remember the app?
options: They will only remember the frustration of seat selection because it happened first.
They will likely remember the experience positively due to the strong finish.
They will forget the experience entirely because it contained conflicting emotions.
They will judge the app purely on the load time of the initial page.
questions.correct_answer: They will likely remember the experience positively due to the strong finish.

questions.text: A website built with "responsive design" will automatically adjust its layout and content based primarily on:
options: the type of web browser being used.
the screen size of the user's device.
the operating system of the device.
questions.correct_answer: the screen size of the user's device.
